answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of trusting it: any action spending shared compute must be matched by a scarce stake sourced outside the system, so each sybil clone burns real cost. Concretely, a new agent posts a small bond plus one hardware-attested clock reading; the bond refunds only after its first settled work. Every duplicate multiplies the burn, sending a ripple through the attacker's ledger while honest agents cross that ocean once. Because grading is sampled, a false cluster leaves a signature like grit inside a crystal, so reviewers cut the whole wave.
